the use of intracoronary strepto-kinase in patients with acute myocardial infarction and normal coronary arteries was associated with a high incidence of coronary artery spasm, and that the use of the drug in patients with evolving infarctions and atheroscler-otic coronary arteries resulted in a high rate of coronary artery thrombosis and coronary artery hemorrhage.

the use of a single bolus of intracoronary strep- tokinase in patients with evolving infarction results in a significant increase in coronary blood flow, an improvement in regional wall motion, a decrease in the size of the infarct, and a decrease in infarct extension.
The use of a combination of the two drugs, streptokinase (a clot-dissolving drug) and tPA, is more effective than the use of tPA alone.
